theme: retry backoff compound PARSEMS + MS2SEC/SEC2MS + SLEEP ms bridge

weaknesses.title: SLEEP unit is milliseconds — easy to confuse with wall seconds
weaknesses.detail: SLEEP 2 pauses ~2ms not 2s. Agents bridging REMAINING seconds must SEC2MS first. Proof labels SLEEP_MS. Silent near-no-op if seconds assumed.

weaknesses.title: MS2SEC floors; SEC2MS(MS2SEC(x)) loses sub-second remainder
weaknesses.detail: 2s500ms → MS2SEC 2 → SEC2MS 2000 (lost 500ms). DEADLINE bridge drops fractional seconds; SLEEP must keep original PARSEMS ms.

weaknesses.title: MS2SEC 999→0 hides sub-second delays for second-scale APIs
weaknesses.detail: Any delay <1s becomes 0 seconds for DEADLINE/SLEEP-if-misused. No CEILMS or ROUND_SECS.

weaknesses.title: Bare digits still milliseconds after compound fix
weaknesses.detail: PARSEMS 60 → 60ms. Compound 1h30m fixed but bare-number unit policy unchanged.

weaknesses.title: NUM still partial-parses trailing junk
weaknesses.detail: max 3x → NUM OK LAST_N=3; agents need pure STR(NUM)==input check (board does).

weaknesses.title: No SLEEP_SEC alias — only MS unit
weaknesses.detail: Must remember SEC2MS pipeline. Easy footgun for ops agents.

workarounds: SLEEP always with PARSEMS ms or SEC2MS(seconds)
Keep original delay_ms for SLEEP; use MS2SEC only for DEADLINE
Reject delays that MS2SEC to 0 when second-scale needed
Pure-digit check for NUM; unit suffixes for PARSEMS
DRY mode for long backoff in tests
language_gaps: SLEEP_SEC / dual unit flag for SLEEP
issues_faced: SLEEP is ms — core lesson for backoff agents
